{"notes": "Visit 4 (8:30): The picture still shows the whole fish dark. Both body arcs, the tail junction (~x23) and both tail fins are connected, with no pale or detached pieces and no hands on the table. That matches the team's 'finished' claim. I still never saw who placed what, so individual credit rests on self-reports and how well they agree. The tail joint is dense and could be fragile at the push. The push is the real test.

Priya: Gave the clear status update (run splits round the body and carries to both tail fins, hands off, restand only what's bumped). Consistent with earlier notes: led the plan, laid the top line, fixed the tail joint. Leadership and ownership are high. Caveat: checks were visual only, and she was a bit confident ('tail joint is clean').

Tom: Silent this visit, third visit running. His '98 of 98' count now also comes from Maya, so it is plausibly a shared figure, but I haven't verified it. Still unwitnessed. Moderate rating, pending the push. Note his low visibility with me.

Leo: Silent this visit, but his earlier overview and status update were strong. Likely did the lower tail (Priya and Tom both say so). Good coordination and collaboration.

Maya: Told me privately that she did the bottom body line and checked the nose split, and that Priya checked the tail joint. This matches others' accounts and the picture. Reliable, clean work and a sensible hands-off stance. More forthcoming one-to-one than publicly, but still low on initiative and leadership.

Shared gap: everyone verified by eye only, and nobody tested the joint."}
